title: Joan Laporta re-elected as Barcelona president with 68 per cent of vote
content:
Joan Laporta has been re-elected as Barcelona’s president.

The 63-year-old won 68 per cent of Sunday’s vote, while his only opponent Victor Font, whom Laporta also beat in 2021, picked up 30 per cent. The rest of the votes were void or invalid.

Font, a 53-year-old fintech entrepreneur, described his candidacy as a chance for a fresh start at Barca, and had promised to bring in a new team of sporting directors.

But it was Laporta who triumphed, extending his stewardship at the club into a fourth term, having also served as Barca president from 2003-2010.

Some 114,504 Barcelona members were eligible to vote in the elections. The turnout was 42.34 per cent — 48,480 members — including head coach Hansi Flick, with multiple players such as Pau Cubarsi and Dani Olmo also participating.

“This is a fantastic win,” Laporta said at the vote announcement in Camp Nou. “It gives us plenty of strength, and makes us unstoppable. The upcoming years are going to be exciting, I am sure they will be some of the best in our lives.

“I can only thank Barca, as a club. An institution in which all members can chose whoever represents them. This is marvellous and unique in the world.”

“In this election, the opposing candidacy came with an idea of confrontation between all Barca fans. Today, the members voted for us because, together, we will defend Barca against everyone and everything. This win is a show of support to the work we have been doing for years.

“It is also fantastic to see our manager, Hansi Flick, who has been a club member and wanted to make the effort to come and vote, and participate to what Barca is.”

Analysis by Barcelona correspondent Pol Ballús

This is a compelling victory for Laporta, and one that rewards the sporting success the team achieved under Hansi Flick.

The results of his latest tenure on the pitch are indisputable. When Laporta was re-elected back in 2021, he inherited a struggling and unbalanced squad and a disastrous financial situation, worsened by the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic. Five years later, Barca are defending champions of a domestic treble in Spain, and seen as one of the best squads in Europe.

That is, deep down, what won him the elections. The emergence of Lamine Yamal, Pau Cubarsi, Marc Bernal and Fermin Lopez came under his leadership. Some might argue those talents were part of the club before Laporta arrived in 2021. But it’s been him who placed the right people in charge to provide those players with the perfect platform to shine.

Victor Font had a (sort of) dream scenario coming to this vote — he was the only alternative to the last president. Font tried to frame this election as a choice between supporting Laporta or supporting Barcelona. But not even the prospect of unifying everyone against him was enough.

The years of Laporta management have also been marked by controversy and money troubles. The creative financial solutions he and his board have developed — they would say as a necessity in response to the situation they inherited from previous president Josep Maria Bartomeu — introduced the word palancas, or ‘levers’, to world football.

But he had a lot in his favour. Hansi Flick expressed his support for the president by attending an event during his campaign. The vast majority of the dressing room was also keen on him staying. Multiple Barca players attended to vote after their match against Sevilla. All of them went to the voting stations flanked by Laporta. The likes of Pau Cubarsi, Marc Bernal, Marc Casado, Gerard Martin, Raphinha, Gavi and Araujo even danced with him.

Now all Barca fans are set to have five years more of Laporta, and the assured continuity of the project led by Flick and Deco. Whether the same level of success is replicated in the upcoming years is yet to be seen.
